current.text: He re-signed with Washington on a 4-year, 213 million deal.

He is Washington's starting point guard and handles the ball the most. Carrington is not the starter. His role is secure. Projected starters are Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr.
In his 5 games with Washington, his usage went down and his assist rate went up.

Experts expect his usage to drop, because Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa share the ball with him. One projection is about 29% usage, and he will not get back to the 37 to 38% of his peak. Experts still expect double-digit assists.
He should play about 33 to 35 minutes, around 7 more per night than last season, so he should beat last season's finish. Experts doubt he gets back to 36 minutes.
With more minutes, his rebounds could rise to about three per game.
His efficiency in his short season (69% at the rim, 62 true shooting) is not expected to hold. If it did hold over 35 minutes, he would be close to a top-15 player.
His FT% dip had no clear cause, and he is projected back at about 86%.

Experts call him a bust at his Yahoo rank of 18 and do not see him as a top-24 player in category leagues. They would take him in round 3, around picks 24 to 27, or later. Range given: best case 13th, worst case 78th.
Josh sees good value at pick 26 in mock drafts. In those mocks Young went at pick 26 and early in round 3.
Experts are not worried about his health. They warn against overreacting to one injury year.
Washington is trying to compete, with a play-in target of about 40 wins. Late-season rest and minutes cuts should not happen this season.

durable.text: He is one of the best passers in the NBA. Experts call him a top-five passer. Assists are his standout category.
He is a multiple-time All-Star and has consistently put up 20 points and 10 assists.
He is one of the worst defenders in the NBA.
His FG% is low on high volume and he commits many turnovers. Both hurt clearly in category leagues.
In category leagues his weak spots outweigh his strong assists.
He is closer to a 35% three-point shooter than a 38% one. Other concerns are his low rebounds and blocks.
He is not injury prone. Last season is the only one where he missed real time, and that time was overstated.

note: Experts see him as a round-3 player, about picks 24 to 27, so the Yahoo value of 38 USD and the 44 USD our league paid last season are too high. The ESPN average cost of about 33 USD is closer to fair. He fits best in punt FG% and punt TO builds, where his assists (z +3.8), FT% (+2.0), points and threes count fully. Early in the season, check that he plays 33 or more minutes and keeps double-digit assists next to Davis and Dybantsa, and watch whether his FG% falls back to about 42%.
